explanation.en:
〜ました is the polite past form of verbs in the ます style. It means “did” or “went,” and it is used for actions that already happened.

Key points:
• Replace ます with ました to make the past
• Polite and common in conversation
• Used for completed actions
• Time words often show when it happened

For example, “食べます” becomes “食べました” (ate). “行きます” becomes “行きました” (went).

You can add time words to make it clear: “昨日行きました” means “I went yesterday.” “先週勉強しました” means “I studied last week.”

The word order stays the same; only the verb ending changes. This makes it easy to shift a present sentence into the past.

Practice by taking simple ます sentences and changing ます to ました. This is one of the most useful and frequent patterns in polite Japanese.

examples.japanese: 先週日本へ行きました。
examples.english: I went to Japan last week.

examples.japanese: 友だちと勉強しました。

commonMistakes.mistake: Using ます with past time words
commonMistakes.correction: Use ました for past actions
commonMistakes.example: ❌ 昨日行きます → ✅ 昨日行きました

commonMistakes.mistake: Dropping ました in polite speech
commonMistakes.correction: Keep ました to stay polite
commonMistakes.example: ❌ 食べたです → ✅ 食べました
